questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to look after twins
The trend of women having babies later in life
Why families in India are getting bigger than before
Health problems that babies have at birth
questions.why: They discuss the trend for older mums and ask, “when are you too old to have a baby?”

questions.q: What reasons for the trend of older mothers does Neil mention?
options: Cheaper healthcare and longer holidays
Pressure from grandparents
New laws about marriage
Better access to education and careers
questions.why: He says the reasons include better access to education and careers.

questions.q: What has Professor Joyce Harper found?
options: In many countries women now have their first baby after 30
Women today are having more babies than before
Most women have their first baby before 20
Older mothers are now completely accepted in every single country
questions.why: She says in many countries women have their first birth over the age of 30.

questions.q: What does Neil say about attitudes to older mothers?
options: People have always admired them
The word “geriatric” is still commonly used by doctors today
An offensive label has gone, but some disapproval remains
Nobody cares about a mother's age any more
questions.why: He says the term “geriatric” is no longer used, but social disapproval still lingers.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention Mick Jagger?
options: To show that men can become fathers much later in life
To give an example of a famous woman who became a mother late
To show that musicians have big families
To say that older fathers are criticised
questions.why: He explains men's fertility lasts longer; Jagger had his eighth child at 73.

questions.q: According to Professor Harper, how do people usually react to a very old father?
options: They feel uncomfortable
They are worried about the baby
They congratulate him
They ignore it
questions.why: She says most people would “pat him on the back”.

questions.q: How does Professor Harper say people react to a woman having a baby in her sixties or seventies?
options: They are pleased and very supportive of her
They think it's normal
They say it's a medical miracle
They are shocked and feel uncomfortable
questions.why: She says it causes a shock reaction and makes people feel uncomfortable.

questions.q: What are many young Gen Z women in the west saying?
options: They want to have children very young
They won't have children at all
They will wait until their fifties
They want large families
questions.why: Beth says Gen Z women are saying they won't have children at all.
